scope: Conditional domain-modeling advisories, no autofix; preserve every accepted state and external contract.

upstreamOwnership.compiler: Existing strict/exact-optional/indexed-access policy remains the owner of compiler guarantees.
upstreamOwnership.exhaustiveness: Existing typescript-eslint switch-exhaustiveness-check and never/assert_never consumers; no duplicate detector.
upstreamOwnership.relatedRules: Existing nominal-ID, closed-set, unsafe-cast and parsed-boundary rules remain the owners of those constraints.

performance.selection: First 200 immutable Standards files sorted by SHA256 of seed 20261016 plus colon plus relative path; all labeled seeds included.
limitations: Every sample starts a fresh bounded process. OS caches are not flushed; first versus repeated process observations are not controlled cold-cache measurements.
Measurements ran on a shared machine alongside other verification; signed differences are observations, not a speedup claim or a hard fleet regression bound.

TypeScript uses the actual selected ESLint rule and full plugin registry; Python compares one shared parsed PythonFileContext per file with and without the selected rule, keeping parsing equal. Full corpus uses the public analyze runner separately.

performanceDecision.metric: Fresh-process elapsed samples, followed by a controlled warmed TypeScript CPU/elapsed comparison on the same bounded panel.
performanceDecision.outcome: The warmed CPU/elapsed followup does not reproduce a greater-than-25-percent analysis regression. The TypeScript fresh-process elapsed result remains load-sensitive and inconclusive. No speedup or fleet guarantee.
performanceDecision.refinement: Normalized model_validator presence gates expensive Python provenance analysis; the fixed 202-file panel enters it for 2 files instead of 21. Unicode aliases and diagnostic spans are preserved.

canonicalValidation.makeVerify: pass across all canonical targets; successful prerequisites reused on resumption
canonicalValidation.githubCI: Required on the exact reviewed PR head before administrative merge; public check results are attached to the PR.
canonicalValidation.typecheck: pass for every package, zero errors and warnings
canonicalValidation.performanceRetry: The unchanged prefer-match-type-dispatch rule exceeded its relative wall-time outlier threshold once in the full Python run under shared load. Both Python performance tests passed on isolated retry; no existing rule or threshold was changed.
canonicalValidation.resumption: All successful canonical prerequisites were retained after correcting the TypeScript helper structure. TypeScript build/lint/typecheck/full dogfood were rerun on the final helper; make typecheck and the remaining make verify targets run separately. No committed gate was weakened.

reproduce.corpus: Use the owner-readable corpus-runner.py, pinned manifests, artifact hashes and performance-runner.py in the local domain-type-safety-20261016 evidence directory. Private overlays are deliberately not published.

limitations: Zero false positives is scoped to the labeled cases and every inspected live match in these exact snapshots; it is not a proof for unseen source.

Corpus snapshots include current tracked working-tree content, pinned both by full Git revision where available and by content digest; installed mature public packages are exact local content snapshots rather than complete upstream repositories.

Only the selected rule runs in each corpus worker; the full registry is imported. TypeScript uses syntax parsing without project-service type information. Full preset interactions are validated separately by repository tests.

Each bounded batch starts a fresh process, using the default 250-file cap plus the 64 KiB argv cap. Startup, full-registry import, parsing and concurrent local work affect process time; these observations do not establish a speedup or a fleet performance guarantee.
Operating-system caches were not flushed. First and repeated runs are fresh-process observations, not controlled cold-cache benchmarks.

Python matching deliberately abstains on opaque/custom payload aliases, inherited models and unsupported validators. TypeScript matching proves producer key presence, not payload validity or all legal states of a shared type.
No autofix can safely choose domain variants, compatibility policy or runtime validation. Existing legacy boolean-result name matching is conditional review guidance, now consistently warning-level.

compilerMatrix.outcome: pass; the shared-policy regression additionally verifies exact optional rejection of explicit undefined

behaviorEquivalence.scope: Pure TypeScript helper refactor, compared with the exact pre-refactor artifact; not additional independent domain labels.

controlledTypescriptFollowup.selection: First 200 immutable Standards files sorted by SHA256 of seed 20261016 plus colon plus relative path; all labeled seeds included.
limitations: One bounded immutable corpus panel per fresh worker; repeated passes within that worker measure warmed parser/rule execution, not independent source coverage.

All modes warm once before measurements; each pass reparses the same inputs and constructs a fresh Linter, and garbage collection runs before each timed pass. Parsing and GC during the timed operation remain included.
CPU measurements reduce scheduling noise; elapsed measurements still share machine resources. No controlled cold-cache or fleet performance guarantee is inferred.
